title: What If a Country Scrapped Its Penny? Canada Did

scenes.text: What if a whole country scrapped its penny? Canada did, and shops didn't collapse.
Each Canadian penny cost nearly 1.6 cents to make. The government was losing money on every coin.
Finance Minister Jim Flaherty struck the very last penny on May 4, 2012, in Winnipeg.
From February 2013, the Mint stopped sending pennies to banks. Old ones stayed legal, if shops took them.
Cash totals now round to the nearest five cents. A total of $1.57 becomes $1.55.
Card payments still settle to the exact cent. The government expected to save about $11 million a year.

description:
What if a country scrapped its penny?
Canada stopped making pennies in 2012 because each cost nearly 1.6 cents to produce, and expected to save about $11 million a year.
